newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina sets tourism record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina sets tourism record in 1996.

text.p: South Carlina's tourism industry logged 32 million visitors who spent $6 billion in 1996, a record even though hurricanes Bertha and Fran temporarily shut down oceanfront resorts, Gov. David Beasley said.
That compared with 31.7 million visitors who spent $6 billion in 1995, the governor said Wednesday at a tourism conference in Fort Mill.
Tourism provided $459 million in state and local tax revenues in 1996, Beasley said.

"Every time a Bertha or Fran strikes, the magnitude of what tourism means to this state hits home, when one lost day cold mean at least $14 million in lost revenue and hundreds of thousands of lives threatened," he said.
